epic.title: Adapter Pattern (post-v1)
epic.description: Post-v1 implementations of the issuance adapter pattern (spec §10, roadmap Phase 9): an AWS Private CA adapter, a reference adapter SDK for third-party CAs, and the adapter health/observability and admin surface (CLI + UI + chaos/runbook obligations). Everything builds strictly on the v1 EntryIntake seam owned by ca-service (anchor entry-intake-trait, §10.2) — no ticket here redefines that trait. Per §1 non-goals (no production cloud spend) everything runs on a laptop against LocalStack and the local demo environment; CDK work is validated by `cdk synth` assertions only, and real-AWS validation is explicitly out of scope. All tickets are priority 3, phase 9.

tickets.title: Reference adapter SDK core crate (adapter-sdk)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/adapter-sdk/`, the reference SDK third-party CA adapters build on (§10, §24 Phase 9). Provides the `Adapter` trait, a runtime harness for event-driven and polling sources, idempotent retry, a policy hook, and submission via the v1 `EntryIntake` seam (§10.2). This ticket consumes that seam; it does not modify it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `crates/adapter-sdk/` exposing an `Adapter` trait covering the §10.3 responsibilities: source subscription (event-driven or polling), policy decision hook, entry construction, submission, and source-specific retry/idempotency
- Runtime harness runs any `Adapter` as a long-lived task with graceful shutdown and backoff on source errors
- All submissions flow through the v1 `EntryIntake` interface with `source_type`/`source_id` populated for audit traceability (§10.2); resubmitting the same `source_id` is idempotent (no duplicate entries)
- Adapter registry holds heterogeneous adapters as `Vec<Arc<dyn Adapter>>` per §22.7 dispatch guidance
- Unit tests against an in-memory `EntryIntake` stub: happy path, transient-error retry, `source_id` dedup, policy rejection

## Out of Scope
- X.509 re-encoding helpers (adapt-x509-reencode)
- AWS PCA adapter, metrics/health surface, admin commands (separate tickets)
- Any change to the `EntryIntake` trait itself (owned by ca-service, v1)

## Testing
- Unit (in-memory stub, §19.1); property test (proptest, §19.2 style): arbitrary crash/retry interleavings never produce duplicate submissions for one `source_id`

## Demo
`cargo test -p adapter-sdk`; then `make demo` with the bundled no-op adapter submitting a canned entry, visible via `mtcctl batch list`.

tickets.title: X.509 to TBSCertificateLogEntry re-encoding helpers
tickets.description:
## Goal
Library helpers that re-encode an existing X.509 certificate from a source CA into a spec-compliant `TBSCertificateLogEntry` (§10.1, §10.3 responsibility 3) — the Cloudflare-playground pattern of logging existing certs as MTC entries. Lives in `crates/adapter-x509/` so it parallelizes with adapt-sdk-core.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Function mapping an X.509 cert (DER and PEM) — subject, SANs, validity, SPKI — into MTC assertion/claim types from core-mtc-types
- Unsupported or unmappable certs return typed errors; no panics on any input
- Round-trip: produced entries satisfy `parse(serialize(x)) == x` via mtc-serialization (§19.2)
- Fixture corpus: RSA and ECDSA certs, multiple DNS SANs, IP SANs, edge-case validity windows
- Fuzz target on the X.509 ingestion path per §19.3 (parser never panics on arbitrary bytes), wired into the existing `fuzz/corpus/` layout

## Out of Scope
- Policy decisions about which certs to log (SDK policy hook)
- Source CA connectivity, authentication, event handling

## Testing
- Unit, property (round-trip, §19.2), fuzz (§19.3)

## Demo
`cargo run -p adapter-x509 --example reencode < fixtures/example.pem` prints the resulting TBSCertificateLogEntry as JSON.

tickets.title: Example dir-watch adapter + add-adapter guide
tickets.description:
## Goal
Prove the SDK's public API with a minimal reference adapter — watches a local directory for PEM files, re-encodes them, submits to the log — and ship the "add a new external CA adapter" guide the spec calls for (§23.1 `add-adapter.md` seeded skill; §25.7 dev-experience tickets are first-class).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Example adapter built purely on the public adapter-sdk API (no internal imports), demonstrating each §10.3 responsibility
- Dropping a PEM into the watched directory yields a logged entry with `source_type="example-dir"` and traceable `source_id` (§10.2)
- `docs/add-adapter.md` and `.claude/skills/add-adapter.md` walk through building an adapter end-to-end using the example as the template (§23.1)
- `make demo-adapter` target wires the example adapter into the local dev environment (§18)
- E2E test: drop cert fixture, entry appears in a batch, inclusion proof verifies

## Out of Scope
- Production sources (AWS PCA, Cloudflare, Keyfactor)
- Adapter pause/metrics/UI (separate tickets)

## Testing
- Unit; E2E via CLI driving the demo environment (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-adapter`, copy `fixtures/example.pem` into the watch dir, then `mtcctl cert lookup` shows the entry with its adapter source fields.

tickets.title: AWS Private CA adapter (Lambda handler)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the first real adapter (§24 Phase 9; OQ-12 selects AWS Private CA as lowest-friction): consume PCA issuance events, fetch the issued cert, apply policy, re-encode, and submit via EntryIntake. Runs as a Lambda per §10.3 (event-driven source) and §5 compute table ("Adapter services | Lambda or Fargate").

## Acceptance Criteria
- Lambda handler consumes EventBridge PCA issuance events (CloudTrail `IssueCertificate` pattern), fetches the cert via `GetCertificate`, and applies the SDK policy hook
- Re-encodes via adapter-x509; submits with `source_type="aws-pca-adapter"` and `source_id` = certificate ARN (§10.2)
- Idempotent on redelivered events: the same ARN is never logged twice (§10.3)
- Authenticates with short-lived IAM credentials (§10.3); no long-lived secrets in code or config
- Transient `GetCertificate` errors retried with backoff; poison events routed to a DLQ path with a failure metric
- Integration tests run against LocalStack with synthetic EventBridge fixtures and stubbed PCA responses — no real AWS (§1 non-goals)

## Out of Scope
- CDK infrastructure (adapt-aws-pca-cdk)
- Cloudflare/Keyfactor/EJBCA adapters; health UI

## Testing
- Unit (policy, idempotency, error mapping); integration against LocalStack (§19.1); E2E in demo env (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo` then `scripts/simulate-pca-issue.sh` injects a synthetic issuance event; `mtcctl batch list` shows the new entry sourced from aws-pca-adapter.

tickets.title: CDK construct for PCA adapter (synth assertions only)
tickets.description:
## Goal
CDK (TypeScript) construct wiring the PCA adapter as spec'd (§5 compute table: adapter services on Lambda; §10.3 event-driven source): EventBridge rule on PCA issuance events, Lambda, DLQ, least-privilege IAM. Laptop-only per §1 non-goals — validated via `cdk synth` assertions, never deployed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Construct in the CDK app composing: EventBridge rule (CloudTrail `IssueCertificate` pattern) -> PCA adapter Lambda -> SQS DLQ
- IAM role limited to `acm-pca:GetCertificate` plus intake-submission permissions; no wildcard resources
- Adapter stack is opt-in via CDK context flag (post-v1 feature, off by default; default synth output unchanged)
- Jest assertion tests verify the event pattern, DLQ wiring, environment config, and least-privilege policy statements

## Out of Scope
- Deployment to real AWS; any AWS spend
- The Lambda application code itself (adapt-aws-pca)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion unit tests (jest) per project calibration; no integration layer (no real AWS, §1)

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK app passes; `cdk synth --context enablePcaAdapter=true` renders the adapter stack to the terminal.

tickets.title: Adapter health and metrics surface
tickets.description:
## Goal
Build the adapter health/observability surface (§24 Phase 9): per-adapter intake counts, success rate, and lag (§20.3 Adapter activity report; §20.1 `entries_by_source_total` metric labeled by source_type), per-source intake rates for the log inventory dashboard (§20.2), and adapter registry health state exposed via an internal admin API route for health-style consumption (§17.2, §20.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- SDK runtime emits per-adapter metrics: intake count, success/failure counts, policy-reject count, source lag, last-success timestamp (§20.1, §20.3)
- Adapter registry exposes a health snapshot (running / paused / erroring, per-adapter rates) via an internal admin API route (§17.2) that the admin surface and health-style checks can read, following the §20.5 health-endpoint convention
- Paused state is persisted so it survives service restart
- Metrics flow into the local dev metrics view (§18) with per-source intake rates matching §20.2's always-visible dashboard list
- Unit tests: emission on success, failure, and policy rejection; health state transitions including erroring -> running recovery

## Out of Scope
- CLI/UI rendering of this data (adapt-admin-surface)
- Alerting/SLO thresholds (observability epic)

## Testing
- Unit; integration (§19.1): example adapter running in the demo env produces observable per-adapter metrics

## Demo
Run `make demo-adapter`, then curl the adapter-health API route: JSON shows per-adapter status, intake counts, and lag.
deps: EXTERNAL:metrics + health-endpoint conventions from self-auditor/observability epic

tickets.title: mtcctl adapter commands, API routes, and Adapters UI page
tickets.description:
## Goal
Full CLI/UI parity (§17.1) for adapter operations: `mtcctl adapter list|status|pause` (§17.3) and the Adapters UI view showing per-adapter health and intake rate (§17.4), backed by new admin API routes both consume (§17.5). Decomposes into ~2 shippable PRs: read routes (list/status) across API+CLI+UI, then the pause/resume mutation path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin API routes (OpenAPI-first, through the §17.2/17.5 codegen pipeline) for adapter list, status, pause, and resume (resume complements the spec'd §17.3 pause); pause is privileged and honors `--confirm`/`--yes` semantics (§17.3)
- `mtcctl adapter list` and `status` show per-adapter health, intake rate, and lag; `--output json` supported for agents (§17.3)
- `mtcctl adapter pause <name>` halts that adapter's intake without losing already-queued entries; state visible in `status` and reversible via resume
- Adapters UI page (htmx + Askama) renders per-adapter health and intake rate with SSE live updates (§17.4)
- CLI and UI exercise the same API routes per the §17.5 end-to-end pattern
- E2E: pause example adapter, drop a PEM (nothing logged), resume, entry logged

## Out of Scope
- Metric collection itself (adapt-health-metrics)
- New adapter implementations

## Testing
- Unit (handlers, CLI arg parsing); integration; E2E via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-adapter`, open the Adapters UI page, then `mtcctl adapter pause example-dir --confirm` and watch status flip in both CLI and UI.

tickets.title: chaos-adapter-flood scenario + adapter-flood runbook
tickets.description:
## Goal
Prove intake backpressure under adapter flood: implement the `chaos-adapter-flood` scenario (§19.9: "Backpressure works; no entries lost") and write the required adapter-flood runbook (§21.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Flood-generator adapter (built on adapter-sdk) drives EntryIntake at a configurable multiple of normal rate against the local demo environment
- Scenario asserts backpressure engages: submitters receive throttle/retry errors rather than silent drops, and queue depth stays bounded
- Scenario asserts zero loss: every accepted entry appears in a committed batch (accepted count == logged count)
- Runs via the chaos harness make target and is registered in the scheduled CI chaos job (§19.9)
- `docs/runbooks/adapter-flood.md` per §21.2 structure: detection signals (per-adapter lag and intake-rate metrics, §20.3), mitigation steps (`mtcctl adapter pause`), and recovery verification

## Out of Scope
- The chaos harness framework itself (testing-infrastructure epic)
- Other chaos scenarios from the §19.9 table

## Testing
- Chaos/E2E (§19.9) in the demo env; unit tests for the flood generator's rate control

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=adapter-flood` prints a report: backpressure engaged, accepted == logged, zero entries lost.
deps: EXTERNAL:chaos test harness from testing-infrastructure epic
